claims.text: Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing revenue, Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion, and AWS's AI and custom-silicon businesses each passed a $25 billion annualized run rate.
Gartner forecasts that by 2028 cloud-native platforms will be the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
AWS reported $42.2 billion revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, accelerating from 28% growth the prior quarter, its fastest growth since 2021.
AWS's AI business and chips business (Trainium and Graviton) each exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate, growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.

Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time; Azure grew 43% year-over-year in fiscal Q4 2026 (ended June 30, 2026), up from 40% the prior quarter; Satya Nadella said 'This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time.'
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026, and its backlog reached $514 billion, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195–205 billion, up from $180–190 billion that had already been raised twice this year.

Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year, with remaining performance obligations of $638 billion, up 363%, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals totaling $75 billion.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure.
Gartner forecasts total worldwide AI spending will reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027 half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.
Gartner predicts that by 2028 over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms, with spending on securing AI reaching roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
Gartner predicts that by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams.

CNCF and SlashData's Q1 2026 Technology Radar found 28% of surveyed organizations have a dedicated platform engineering team and 35% run a hybrid platform combining developer platforms with AI tooling.
Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said developers are standardizing on CNCF projects and organizations are extending those platforms to support AI workloads.
Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029, while human-in-the-loop requirements fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.

Pulumi's 2026 survey: 82% agree AI agents will change how they write infrastructure within 12 months; 63% say they trust agents to make production changes while manual approval remains close to universal; expectation of agents generating half or more of code rises from 45% to 52% in six months.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails.
Mordor Intelligence says the global Kubernetes market is USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.

CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among ML/AI developers at 41%, and 30% of backend developers using Kubernetes, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, which the report attributes to maturity.
Gartner says by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are piloting, deploying or beginning to use them.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a generally available MCP server for its Agent Toolkit, and Mirantis's Lens launched a built-in MCP server.
Gartner predicts 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
The post is updated for 2027 and the 2026 edition's predictions held up.
